messages.subject: Identification problem in bfactor
parts:
Hi Phil and others,

I'm trying to estimate a bifactor model with 5 specific factors using bfactor (shown below). There are 85 items in the dataset. When I set SE=TRUE (with the default SE.type="crossprod"), I receive an error that the information matrix cannot be inverted. I thought I had specified the model correctly (following the examples). Did I miss a necessary identification constraint? Or is this some other issue (such as empirical underidentification or an issue with the estimation algorithm)? 

Any help would be appreciated.

Thanks, Brenton

Model: 

efa5d = c(4, 3, 1, 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 5, 2, 2, 1, 1, 3, 2, 1, 1, 1, 4, 2, 1, 5, 2, 3, 3, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 3, 3, 1, 5, 5, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1, 4, 5, 4, 2, 1, 1, 4, 4, 1, 5, 3, 1, 4, 3, 1, 3, 1, 4, 5, 3, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 5, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 1, 1, 2)

EGBefa5 = bfactor(A, efa5d, itemtype="graded", SE=TRUE, technical = list(NCYCLES=2000))

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Identification problem in bfactor
parts:
Hi Brenton,

This looks to be an empirical identification issue to me as the model is identified (all factors load on at least the items). How large is your sample? Also, you could try other, more stable methods like the Louis approach, but this may take much longer to obtain. Cheers.

Phil

Thanks.

I ran it first using a sample with 499 and then also tried to add an extra 200 (which I had excluded due to substantial group differences). Currently waiting for the larger sample model to finish estimating with Louis information. I'll see if that helps (I know that the sample is rather small for a 2-dimensional graded model--this is an interim analysis).

(Out of curiosity, about how much slower is the Louis method compared to the crossproudct, 2x, 3x, exponential?)

Edit: It estimated correctly when using the Louis estimator. Thanks again.
